correctness.rationale: For any active state, two distinct target centers exist among N spaced by five confidence radii because N-2 other agents each block at most one. Positive finite utilities constrain the deterministic pre-noise moves within three radii of an eligible agent. Independent full-support Gaussians give uniform state-independent probability p of a favorable two-agent isolation. At most floor(N/2) consecutive favorable events absorb; block Markov iteration yields geometric survival and finite expectation. Invariant laws then concentrate on absorbing states. For N=2, mu=1/2, exact disagreement is independent fresh Gaussian difference with erfc exit probability and standard sharp asymptotic. 3,611 reproducible exact-rational/numerical checks support but do not replace proof.

value.rationale: Shows a rigorous noncommuting time-scale boundary between the exact, conditionally perturbed finite opinion model and its single-cluster Gibbs diffusion approximation. The general absorbing-measure classification and state-uniform finite-block tail rule out truly persistent finite-size microscopic within-cluster stationarity; the exact two-agent formula quantifies an exponentially large weak-noise observation window that explains deceptive quasi-stationarity. It clarifies a consequential modeling choice: whether shocks occur on rejected encounters. The value does not rely on model-independent social generalization or a sharp N-agent mean-lifetime bound.
